domain_restrictions: M and U are required to be nonzero polynomials in q with rational coefficients
M and U are required to be coprime in the polynomial ring over the rationals
Loc_M is built from the Laurent polynomial ring in q over the rationals by inverting every polynomial coprime to M
X and Y are required to lie in Loc_M, so they are also rational functions in q
H is required to lie in the Laurent polynomial ring in q over the rationals
The equality U times X minus Y equals M times H is interpreted in the field of rational functions in q
The congruence relation modulo M is defined using the ideal generated by M inside Loc_M
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For any nonzero coprime polynomials M and U over the rationals, if X and Y are elements of the M-localized Laurent polynomial ring and their difference becomes divisible by M after multiplying by U, with the quotient represented by some Laurent polynomial H, then X and Y are congruent modulo M in that localization.
quantifier_order: For all nonzero polynomials M and U in q over the rationals, with gcd of U and M equal to 1
Define Loc_M as the localization of the Laurent polynomial ring in q over the rationals obtained by inverting every polynomial coprime to M
For all X and Y in Loc_M
If there exists H in the Laurent polynomial ring in q over the rationals such that U times the difference X minus Y equals M times H in the rational function field in q
Then X is congruent to Y modulo M, meaning X minus Y lies in the ideal generated by M inside Loc_M

statement_nl: Let M(q) and U(q) be nonzero elements of Q[q] with gcd(U(q),M(q))=1. Let Loc_M be the localization of the Laurent polynomial ring Q[q,q^{-1}] obtained by inverting every polynomial V(q) in Q[q] with gcd(V(q),M(q))=1. For rational functions X(q) and Y(q) in Q(q), write X(q) ≡ Y(q) mod M(q) if X(q)-Y(q) belongs to the ideal M(q)·Loc_M. Assume X(q) and Y(q) both belong to Loc_M. If there exists H(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that U(q)(X(q)-Y(q))=M(q)H(q) in Q(q), then X(q) ≡ Y(q) mod M(q).
